rich_summary: This section captures the final verbal exchanges before the Kurukshetra war begins. Through Uluka, messenger of Duryodhana, the Pandava side delivers fierce responses and vows. Bhima swears to kill Dussasana and drink his blood and to break Duryodhana’s thighs, recalling the humiliation of Draupadi. Other warriors also declare their targets: Sikhandin vows to bring down Bhishma, and Dhrishtadyumna promises to slay Drona. Yudhishthira alone speaks with restraint, regretting the coming slaughter while acknowledging that Duryodhana’s obstinacy has made war inevitable. Uluka returns and reports everything, after which Duryodhana orders the Kaurava armies to be arrayed before sunrise. The scene then shifts to the Pandava camp, where Dhrishtadyumna organizes the army and assigns rival champions to face specific enemies, formally setting the stage for the epic battle.

highlight_spans.why: Opening rebuke warning Duryodhana of the disaster his arrogance and refusal of peace will bring.
Bhima’s terrifying oath to kill Dussasana and drink his blood, one of the most emotionally charged vows in the epic.
Sikhandin’s declaration that he was born to destroy Bhishma, foreshadowing the crucial turning point of the war.
Yudhishthira’s restrained statement that he does not desire the slaughter of his own kin, highlighting the moral tragedy of the conflict.
Duryodhana orders the armies to assemble before sunrise, marking the irreversible step from diplomacy to war.

top_scenes.scene_text: Bhima, furious in the Pandava camp, raises his mace and swears before the warriors that he will slay Dussasana and drink his blood.
Sikhandin standing at the front of the army, pointing toward the Kaurava lines and vowing to bring down the mighty Bhishma.
At dawn preparations, messengers race through the vast Kaurava camp on horses and camels announcing Duryodhana’s command to array the armies for battle.
